description: Our team, composed of students from Kepirtepe Anatolian High School, is an innovation and research group passionate about science and space, dedicated to seeking creative solutions to contemporary challenges. We are confident that the teamwork skills we have cultivated through our projects will be effectively demonstrated at this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge. We will complete our chosen mission—"Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer"—by integrating both physical and logical technologies.
summary:
Our project aims to create an application that facilitates the active development of children aged 7–12, helping them grow into the astronauts of the future by providing access exclusively to authentic and accurate resources.
Through our project, we seek to foster the ability to resolve crises and enhance "reflexive intelligence"—enabling these young individuals to find effective, efficient, and stress-free solutions to challenges, not only within the realm of space exploration but in any difficult situation they may encounter. In doing so, we aim to cultivate a knowledgeable generation, ensuring that valuable insights are preserved and passed on.
details: Our project offers a game simulation for children aged 7–12, designed to be both entertaining and educational. Built on the Scratch platform, the game is accessible to everyone. Children can join for free simply by pasting a link into any web browser. The game introduces them to space and the realities of a space mission—presented in a straightforward, accessible way—while exploring Mars and potentially inspiring them toward future paths. By simulating the real-life consequences of in-game decisions, the project ensures that children have fun while gaining lasting insights. Players control a character and navigate scenarios inspired by daily life—such as energy conservation, water management, or maintaining an ecosystem. Every decision has a consequence: a poor choice leads to the depletion of resources, while a sound decision results in in-game success and an explanation of why that specific knowledge matters. The game begins with simple tasks and gradually increases in analytical complexity, featuring modules that stimulate critical thinking. Ultimately, children see the impact of their own choices, fostering personal growth. In developing this project, we utilized Scratch, incorporating original drawings created by the children themselves on computers and tablets.
